rv.q: Ultimately, though, what makes the show so shockingly tepid is that the hard-working troupe of champion dancers, culled from numerous countries, rarely emit much personality or even find significant ways to connect to each other or the audience.
The accent on high-octane tempos and audience-dazzling athleticism ultimately left me feeling more dazed than elated.
Either way, this is a glorified floor show at Broadway prices.
While there’s only about 15 ounces of collective body fat onstage, there’s also about 15 ounces of imagination.
Two-plus hours of dancing flies by with storytelling and pacing worthy of any Broadway musical.
There's an electrifying finale to 'Proud Mary' that will surely inspire you to cash in the coupon for a free ballroom dance lesson that a local dance studio is distributing outside the theater.
Burn the Floor is an experience that alternates between exhilarating and contrived.
While physically hot, the production is tepid when it comes to dramatic intensity.
It's a thrilling genre, not to be missed for those who love the dance.

cn.t: Critics find this ballroom spectacle flashy and energetic but ultimately more suited to reality TV fans than discerning theatergoers, with impressive dancing undermined by tacky presentation and uneven pacing.

vs.sum: The Longacre Theatre offers good sightlines with minimal obstructions, even from the balcony, and the sound quality is consistently praised. While the seating is a bit narrow, it provides average comfort for most patrons. The theater's ambiance is enhanced by its elegant Beaux Arts interior, and facilities are typical for a Broadway venue, with some lines at intermission but generally manageable.

acc.note: Small restroom-only elevator (may not accommodate all wheelchairs). 3 wheelchair spaces in Orchestra.
